articles.headline: Sources: Sean Payton to expand role in Broncos' playcalling process
articles.description: The Broncos are taking a more collaborative playcalling approach this week with coach Sean Payton having an increased role in the process, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos will take a more collaborative playcalling approach Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers as the team looks to kick-start a sputtering offense, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

Coach Sean Payton, who surrendered the playcalling duties to first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb during the offseason, will have an increased role in the game-day operation, the sources said. Webb is expected to still be on the headset as the voice quarterback Bo Nix hears before each play.

Payton, who has remained a large presence in the game-planning and offensive meetings even after ceding playcalling to Webb earlier this year, is expected to be more active on the headsets before, and during, the Broncos' possessions than he has been in the first four games. He has previously described the decision-making process through the week with, "I'll be involved, this is still our offense, the Broncos' offense.''

Asked Wednesday if four games constituted a big enough sample size to determine if he might be a better option to call plays to snap out of the early-season struggles, Payton said: "I think our focus needs to be more on the specific and the detail of each play regardless [of who's calling the plays]. I think Davis is very fast, very quick and understands what we're doing.

"I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys. I think, collectively, we all after a game, and after a four-game sample size, certainly this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?''

Payton has repeatedly said in recent weeks he's been frustrated with the team's lack of consistency in the run game as well as their difficulties on first down that has consistently put the offense in difficult down-and-distance situations.

The Broncos (2-2) are near the bottom of the league rankings in scoring (27th), total yards per game (27th), rushing yards per game (29th), passing yards per game (20th), QBR (23rd) and Offensive EPA (22nd at -7.48). Only six teams have had more three-and-out possessions than the Broncos this season as 27.5% of their possessions have ended with three plays and a punt.

Nix is also currently ranked 22nd in QBR (46.1) and 27th in average air yards per attempt (5.9) as the lack of big plays on offense has become a four-game trend. The Broncos, overall, are 29th in the league in plays of 20 or more yards and 30th in explosive plays with 16 (runs of at least 10 yards and pass plays of at least 20 yards).

Payton said Wednesday he believes it all tracks to "the details, the little things,'' rather than some substantial shift in approach on offense as the team prepares to face the Chargers (0-4) Sunday in SoFi Stadium.

"The inconsistencies, the details, the little things,'' Payton said Wednesday. "... Let's focus on the attention to detail and the rest will follow.''

Payton doesn't normally speak publicly to the media

articles.headline: Man City manager Enzo Maresca says he 'trusts the club completely'
articles.description: Enzo Maresca has said he "trusts the club completely" in his first interview since Manchester City were found guilty of breaking financial rules.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca has said he "trusts the club completely" in his first interview since Manchester City were found guilty of breaking financial rules.

Maresca is preparing his players for the trip to Liverpool on Sunday -- City's first game since the publication of the damning judgement in their case with the Premier League.

The Italian spoke to in-house media on Thursday. He's due to hold his first news conference with reporters since the verdict on Friday morning.

"Personally, I'm very calm to be honest," said Maresca.

"The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club.

"We understand the noise, but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side."

Despite the guilty verdict, both chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano have insisted the club are innocent. A formal appeal has been launched.

The bulk of City's players have been away on international duty during the break. Now back at the CFA, Maresca insists they are "focused" despite intense spotlight on the Etihad Stadium.

"The feeling is fantastic, to be honest," Maresca said.

"The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league.

"The players are just focused on that. They know what we can control is the football side -- they are not worried at all about different things.

"They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield."

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Points league draft tiers
articles.description: André Snellings groups players into tiers by each position for points leagues.
articles.body:
In our recent 10-team points mock draft, the first round leaned heavily toward point guards and big men. Four point guards came off the board, along with three power forwards and two centers. Anthony Edwards was the only shooting guard selected, and no small forwards were taken. The first small forward didn't go until Amen Thompson at No. 13 overall, followed by Scottie Barnes and Cooper Flagg later in the second round.

By the middle of the draft, the board looked much different. Round 6 alone featured four small forwards: Caleb Wilson, Brandon Miller, Franz Wagner and Trey Murphy III. That tells you a lot about this year's player pool. Point guards and big men are prominent near the top, while much of the wing depth shows up later. That doesn't mean you have to force a small forward early, but you should know where each position starts to thin out.

Point guard gives you more room to wait. My third tier alone includes Tyrese Maxey, Jalen Brunson, Trae Young, Josh Giddey, Devin Booker, Tyrese Haliburton, James Harden, LaMelo Ball and Jamal Murray. If several of those players are still available, there may be no reason to reach for the position.

Small forward is different. The position has useful depth later, but the top options disappear quickly. Power forward also has a large middle group, while center is more concentrated near the top, with Nikola Jokic in his own tier and Victor Wembanyama right behind him.

This is where the board starts to matter more than the rankings. A straight ranking tells you who I value more. Tiers tell you where the drop-offs are. If several point guards remain in the same tier but only one small forward is left before a drop, that should factor into your pick. The same applies when a position has enough depth to let you wait another round.

The tiers below are based on our preseason projections and show where we see the biggest breaks at each position. The idea is simple: know where you can wait and where waiting too long could cost you.

Point guard

Thoughts on PGs:

Gilgeous-Alexander is projected for 31.3 PPG, 6.4 APG and 1.7 SPG, while Doncic is projected for 33.0 PPG, 8.9 APG and 8.5 RPG. Gilgeous-Alexander has the stronger durability track record, while Doncic brings elite production across points, rebounds and assists.

Cunningham stands alone in Tier 2. He finished sixth in fantasy points per game last season and is projected for 24.6 PPG and 9.8 APG.

The depth starts in Tier 3 with Maxey, Brunson, Young, Giddey, Booker and Haliburton. Haliburton could outperform this group if he returns to form after missing last season.

Harden, Ball and Murray make up Tier 4 and give managers another strong group if they wait at the position. Ball brings plenty of upside in Minnesota, while Harden and Murray remain reliable fantasy options.

There are also a few younger guards worth watching later, including Harper and Acuff Jr.

articles.headline: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman aggravates foot, out weeks
articles.description: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman Jr. aggravated a foot injury and is out multiple weeks.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. aggravated a foot injury in Wednesday's practice, and he will likely be sidelined multiple weeks, coach Mike McCarthy said Thursday.

Pittman had been dealing with plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which led him to miss the Week 2 game against the New England Patriots. The receiver was spotted using a scooter to keep weight off his left foot in the locker room following Wednesday's practice.

"It's the same foot, so it's going to be a multiple-week injury," McCarthy said. "We're still going through the evaluation of his roster position."

The Steelers landed the veteran Indianapolis Colts receiver for a late-round pick swap in a March trade and subsequently signed him to a three-year, $59 million extension. The 2020 second-round pick was productive and versatile in six seasons with the Colts, posting two 1,000-yard seasons. Pittman, though, hasn't been productive early on in his tenure in Pittsburgh, catching just seven passes on 12 targets for 89 yards. The 29-year-old also missed a large chunk of training camp with a separate, undisclosed injury.

Pittman's injury comes as the Steelers prepare to face his former team Sunday -- an occasion that quarterback Aaron Rodgers pointed out in his Wednesday news conference.

"We'd love to get Pitt involved, especially this week, being his former team, but there's going to be opportunities for a lot of guys," Rodgers said.

That rings especially true with McCarthy's assertion that Pittman will miss multiple weeks. Without Pittman, the Steelers will lean more heavily on third-year receiver Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard. Wilson, who was largely uninvolved in the offense during his first two seasons, has become one of Rodgers' go-to targets. He caught touchdown passes in Weeks 3 and 4, marking the first time in his career that he recorded touchdown receptions in consecutive games. Wilson, a 2024 third-round pick, has 14 receptions on 24 targets for 188 yards and is averaging 13.4 yards per reception as a field-stretching target.

"Roman has a second gear that you love to utilize as much as you possibly can," McCarthy said Thursday, adding that Wilson has improved his route-running.

Bernard, a second-round pick out of Alabama, has seven receptions on 11 targets, including eight against the Patriots, for 60 yards.

"Germ has been balling since he first got here," wide receiver DK Metcalf said. "Big kudos to him and his preparation, because like I told him, it's very difficult trying to learn the signals and the offense as well. He's done a hell of a job."

While the Steelers' offense will be down at least one player -- and possibly more with Rico Dowdle continuing to miss practice after twice dislocating a toe in the loss to New England -- the defense could soon be getting a boost. articles.headline: Erling Haaland calls on Man City to 'stay positive' amid Premier League charges case
articles.description: Erling Haaland has said that everyone at Manchester City has to "stay positive" as the team prepares to play their first matches since being found guilty of breaching Premier League regulations.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland has said that everyone at Manchester City has to "stick together" and "stay positive" as the team prepares to play its first match since being found guilty on 100-plus charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. 

Most City players were away representing their respective countries during the extended international break when the outcome of City's legal battle against the Premier League was made public. 

City have branded the verdict "unsafe" and have lodged a "comprehensive appeal" of the independent commission verdict.

- What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

Enzo Maresca's team travels to face Liverpool on Sunday and seems certain to receive a hostile reception from the Anfield crowd. 

"I think they [the City fans travelling to Anfield] are going to have a good time," Haaland told club media.

"We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive.

"No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile. We have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game."

Haaland joined City from Borussia Dortmund in 2022 and has won a host of individual and team honors in the years since. 

"I care a lot about this place -- the UK, generally," he said. "My mother as well [as my father], they lived here for 10 years -- they lived in Nottingham and Leeds.

"They never lived in Manchester, but obviously my father trained over at Carrington every day.

"I spent my first four years here, my brother nine and my sister six, so it's a special place for us.

"I care a lot about City, I have to say.

"I care a lot about the fans because I'm a fan myself -- I feel with them as well."

- Sources: Guardiola set to attend first City home game since guilty verdict

The Norway international added in an interview with Sky Sports: "And no matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile.

"So we have to stay positive, look ahead and then try to win football games and then try to enjoy the situation and the game."

Information from PA contributed to this story.

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

articles.headline: Jayden Daniels will be 'full go' vs. Giants, says Commanders OC
articles.description: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels will have no limitations when the star QB plays Sunday against the Giants.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels will have no limitations when the star quarterback plays Sunday against the New York Giants.

"He's full go," Blough said Thursday when asked if Washington had to account for Daniels' dislocated left elbow in the game plan. "We're looking forward to having him back."

Daniels was a full participant in practice Wednesday and was expected to be one all week with the idea that he'll start Sunday against the Giants (3-1). The Commanders (1-3) have endured another injury-filled season, with Daniels already having missed two games because of his non-throwing elbow injury.

Daniels suffered the injury in Washington's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys; he had initially dislocated it in Week 9 last season.

Because he has suffered the same injury twice, Daniels will wear a black brace that leaves his elbow slightly bent. Last week, Daniels said the brace won't limit him when handing off or taking snaps from center.

The quarterbacks start each practice by taking snaps from under center, and Daniels was doing that last week as well as Wednesday. Daniels said he is getting used to the brace, which is different from the one he wore last season when he returned in Week 14 vs. Minnesota.

Daniels will need to wear the brace the rest of the season. He has talked since training camp opened about being smarter when running in games. His game has been built on dynamic play -- running when needed, whether designed or scrambling.

articles.headline: What does your NBA team need? The biggest hole on all 30 rosters
articles.description: Every NBA team is missing something, even the leading title contenders.
articles.headlineJa: あなたのNBAチームに足りないものは？ 全30チームのロスターにおける最大の弱点
articles.descriptionJa: 優勝候補の有力チームであっても、すべてのNBAチームには何かしらの欠けている要素がある。
articles.body:
In the NBA's second apron era, deep rosters don't stay deep forever, team identities can flip at a moment's notice, and money can prompt painful divorces.

This summer alone, the 2026 champion New York Knicks lost beloved backup center Mitchell Robinson, the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder shed three rotation players in cost-cutting trades, and the 2024 champion Boston Celtics traded away Finals MVP Jaylen Brown. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Timberwolves sacrificed frontcourt depth to assemble a tantalizing backcourt duo, and LeBron James said goodbye to the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons.

Let's take stock of all 30 teams now that the offseason dust has settled and the preseason is in full swing. With so many salary cap rules preventing teams from aggregating talent, everybody is missing something, even the leading title contenders. But what, exactly, is each team's biggest hole?

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

Roster hole: Superstar centerpiece

The Hawks have methodically constructed a balanced rotation with healthy doses of ballhandling, outside shooting and on-ball defense. After adding championship experience by nabbing Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins from the Oklahoma City Thunder in offseason trades, Atlanta's biggest question is whether Jalen Johnson can elevate from All-Star to superstar.

The do-everything forward saw his impressive regular-season numbers dip dramatically in a first-round series loss to the Knicks, but he's still only 24 years old. Can he develop into an offensive fulcrum capable of leading a deep playoff run?

The Hawks can be patient in their assessment as they boast enough salary cap flexibility and draft assets to explore a big-name addition down the road.

Johnson is entering the second year of a team-friendly extension worth $150 million over five seasons, and none of Atlanta's other core pieces are on the books for more than $25 million this season.

Boston Celtics

Roster hole: Free throw generator

While the Celtics' decision to trade Brown for Paul George made sense as a long-term financial play, it created two immediate problems on the court. First, the 36-year-old George played less than half as many minutes as the 29-year-old Brown last season. Second, George attempted only 111 free throws in 2025-26 -- a far cry from Brown's 536, which easily represented a career high.

George's perimeter shooting and experience playing off high-usage stars should make him a good fit next to Jayson Tatum in coach Joe Mazzulla's 3-point heavy system, but Boston will need to find a way to replace Brown's ability to work inside the arc and draw contact. The Celtics ranked last in free throw attempts last season even though Brown ranked fifth in the NBA.

articles.headline: What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take
articles.description: Man City have appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board also begins its work on figuring out appropriate punishments. So what happens next, and what is the possible timeline?
articles.body:
Manchester City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission's guilty verdict of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period, and the waiting game now begins again for the final outcome of the investigation.

But the judgment of the independent panel -- made up of judges and independent financial and legal experts -- which was published on Sept. 29, 21 months after the culmination of a 12-week hearing, marked the end of the beginning of an investigative process dating back to 2019.

The appeal process heralds the beginning of the end, and sources have told ESPN that a time frame is in place for City's fate -- guilty or innocent -- to be resolved by the end of this season.

The club, which continues to protest its innocence citing "irrefutable evidence," could yet take the case beyond sporting regulatory bodies to the High Court in the United Kingdom if the appeal fails and City can prove serious irregularities in the Premier League's disciplinary process.

- Man City found guilty: All features, analysis, reaction

But now that City's appeal has been set in motion, both the club and Premier League are approaching the end of a long and difficult road. So what happens next? When will this all be over and what are the sanctions that City could face?

The appeals process

Man City had 14 days after being officially informed of the verdict from the independent commission to serve notice of their decision to appeal. The club did so on Oct 1. A new three-person independent panel, appointed by Sir Gary Hickinbottom (High Court judge and former UK Lord Justice of Appeal), will be formed as an Appeal Board to review the case.

In Premier League regulations, under Section W of the Premier League Handbook, Appeal Boards must have three members, one of whom should have held judicial office (a judge) and would sit as the chair of the Appeal Board.

The appeal process must be concluded within 12 weeks of the appeal being lodged. If the full 12 weeks are required to hear City's case, it would have to finish by Dec. 25 and the panel must deliver its verdict, according to Premier League regulation W.95, "within 30 days of the final day of the appeal hearing."

This is where the time frame gets tricky. The Christmas and New Year period will signal a two-week holiday shutdown of the legal process, so if the 30-day clock began on Jan. 8, the three-person panel would have until Feb. 8 to announce its verdict.

However, an appeal is not certain. The Appeal Board, as per regulation W.96, must initially decide whether to allow the appeal or dismiss it, but even if City's grounds for appeal are regarded as flimsy, it is unlikely that they would have it rejected due to the magnitude of the case.

The sanctions hearing

articles.headline: Everton's Martin Sherif fined for breaching FA betting rules
articles.description: Everton youngster Martin Sherif has been fined for breaching Football Association betting rules.
articles.body:
Everton youngster Martin Sherif has been fined for breaching Football Association betting rules.

The 20-year-old, who is yet to make a first-team debut for the Toffees, admitted having caused, permitted or enabled 61 bets to be placed on football matches between November 2024 and February this year.

Sherif has avoided a ban but must pay a £5,000 ($6,600) fine.

In his defence, the forward said he had not personally placed any of the bets, which totalled almost £2,000 ($2,600), but admitted they came from accounts in his name.

An independent regulatory commission hearing took into account Sherif's prompt admission of guilt after he was charged in August, his cooperation with the procedure and his "genuine remorse."

Sherif, a Netherlands youth international who joined Everton aged 13, spent last season on loan at Rotherham and Port Vale.

He scored two League One goals for each club across 24 total appearances.

articles.headline: The Warriors need Yaxel Lendeborg's fast-tracked development
articles.description: The Golden State Warriors have high hopes for the No. 11 pick after several failed lottery picks.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズ、ヤクセル・レンデボーグの早期育成を必要としている
articles.descriptionJa: ゴールデンステート・ウォリアーズは、これまでのドラフト・ロトでの失敗が続いたこともあり、指名11位の選手に大きな期待を寄せている。
articles.body:
THE WEEK PRIOR to training camp, every Golden State Warriors player gathered at Jimmy Butler's mansion in San Diego and competed in a handful of pickup games.

In his lone game paired with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green, rookie wing Yaxel Lendeborg found himself near the elbow during a frontcourt inbound. As the ball was delivered to Green up top, Curry cut toward Lendeborg to set a back screen. Both defenders remained with Curry and Lendeborg, sensing it, slipped backdoor and received a pass from Green for an uncontested dunk.

"'That's all year! All year!'" Green and Curry roared at Lendeborg with ferocity, according to the rookie. "Super loud and aggressive."

In Lendeborg's mind, he made the simple read within the flow, using Curry's gravity for two easy points. It represented something far bigger for Green and Curry. Their newest weapon was already recognizing and leveraging the patterns that make the Warriors' offense hum, signaling a readiness to help the team win before the two franchise legends age out of the league.

"It looked like we had been playing together for a long time," Green said.

On their final draft board in June, the Warriors -- who owned the No. 11 pick -- had Lendeborg and Arizona guard Brayden Burries ranked neck-and-neck, behind the consensus group of prospects up top. If Burries was there, team sources have indicated they would've drafted the 20-year-old combo guard for his upside. He had fans all over the organization.

But the Milwaukee Bucks, selecting 10th, took away that option. The Warriors quickly pivoted to Lendeborg, adding the older prospect they believed fit their immediate timeline and urgency of Curry's final seasons.

"He's massive," Butler said. "Just a big human being."

At 24 years old and 241 pounds, standing 6-foot-9 with a 7-foot-4 wingspan, Lendeborg has the size and power of a mid-prime wing on a Warriors roster that is currently thin and injured at that spot, waiting for Butler and Moses Moody to return from lengthy rehabs for serious knee injuries.

Lendeborg won over Steve Kerr in the predraft process, impressing the Warriors coach during a film session because of his knowledge of the game paired with charisma and his willingness to learn.

"Unbelievably coachable," Kerr said after Tuesday night's preseason win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

The organization has been impressed that, after a long national title run at Michigan that included an MCL and ankle sprain in the NCAA tournament, Lendeborg took his offseason work seriously, played in eight summer league games and led them to a Las Vegas title.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ「アーセナルのCL決勝敗戦の傷跡は今も残っている」
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタは、5月に行われたパリ・サンジェルマンとのチャンピオンズリーグ決勝での敗戦による「傷跡」がいまだに残っていると語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

articles.headline: Raúl Asencio on drink driving conviction: 'I'm at Real Madrid, that can't happen again'
articles.description: Raúl Asencio has said he is only focused on winning at Real Madrid and "turning the situation around" following his recent conviction for drink driving.
articles.headlineJa: ラウル・アセンシオ、飲酒運転での有罪判決について語る：「レアル・マドリードにいる身として、二度と同じことは起こさない」
articles.descriptionJa: ラウル・アセンシオは、最近の飲酒運転による有罪判決を受け、レアル・マドリードでの勝利にのみ集中し、「状況を好転させる」と語った。
articles.body:
Raúl Asencio has said he is only focused on winning at Real Madrid and "turning the situation around" following his recent conviction for drink driving.

The Spanish centre-back was fined €14,400 (£12,208 / $16,103) on Sept. 2 and had his driver's licence suspended for eight months having admitted to driving under the influence of alcohol after testing positive at a sobriety checkpoint.

"It was a really tough time," Asencio told Diario AS. "Several things in my life coincided within a short space of time."

One day after his DUI conviction, Asencio was acquitted by a Spanish court of charges related to allegedly recording sexual images of a woman and a minor and distributing them without their consent.

Real Madrid opened a disciplinary proceeding against Asencio after his drink driving conviction, with coach José Mourinho stressing that a "Madrid player is 24 hours a day, seven days a week and 12 months a year."

Asencio, who was promoted to Madrid's first team in the summer of 2024, agreed.

"He [Mourinho] was absolutely right," he said. "Ultimately, people form opinions based on what's reported and what they see. I made a mistake. I admitted it then and I admit it now; I've apologised and I'll continue to do so. I'm a 23-year-old lad and I've made mistakes, just as we all do at that age.

"But I have to be aware of where I am. I'm at Real Madrid and that can't happen again. I'm taking this seriously and my only focus is on turning this situation around. I'm the one who's most upset about it.

- Mourinho already has a lot to do to save Real Madrid's season

- Jude Bellingham hits new heights for England as Tuchel gets best out of Real Madrid star

- Getafe president: Deal for ex-Real Madrid defender Dani Carvajal is off

"I dream of turning it all around and winning trophies with this club and in this shirt -- hopefully for the rest of my career. That's why situations like this won't happen again."

Asencio made 34 appearances for Madrid in the 2025-26 campaign.

Injuries have prevented Asencio from playing for Madrid this season, with the player currently sidelined until next year after having surgery for a stress fracture in his right tibia on Oct. 1.
